result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.coreness()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate k-core decomposition (coreness for each node). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16676-L16745){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.coreness( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The k-core is the maximal subgraph where every node has degree >= k. A node's coreness is the highest k-value for which it belongs to the k-core. Uses iterative pruning: repeatedly removes nodes with degree < k until all remaining nodes have degree >= k. Higher coreness indicates nodes in denser, more cohesive parts of the graph. The k-core decomposition is useful for finding the 'nucleus' of a network. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store coreness values. If `None`, uses `coreness` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to coreness values. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: Dictionary mapping node IDs to coreness values (non-negative integers). If `return_dict=` is `False`: Returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every node in a complete graph K4 is connected to all three others, so removing any one node still leaves a fully-connected triangle behind -- meaning all four nodes share the maximum possible coreness of `3`: ::: {#09c90328 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("A", "D") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("B", "D") .add_edge("C", "D") ) graph.coreness(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 3, 1: 3, 4: 3, 2: 3} ``` ::: :::
